strengths: The virtual-correspondence construction is an original and practically useful way to obtain approximate four-point solvers from established 5-point/6-point and P3P implementations. The mean-based method offers a particularly accessible alternative to complicated algebraic or homotopy solvers. This independently useful contribution is the main reason for weak acceptance.

The experiments demonstrate competitive robust-estimation performance. In Table 1, the mean-plus-shift solver improves Sacre Coeur median error from HC's 3.04° to 2.42° and AUC@10° from 50.61 to 52.27. On KITTI, Table 2 reports comparable or slightly better pose accuracy than 6pt+P3P at 0.07 versus 0.11 seconds.

The evaluation includes 10,000 real image triplets, controlled noise and outlier experiments, shift ablations, several conventional baselines, and informative oracle comparisons. Testing existing four-point solvers alongside the straightforward 5pt+P3P baseline is itself valuable for understanding practical solver choices.

The manuscript clearly acknowledges that its solutions are approximate and that sampling an additional real correspondence can produce better accuracy. Supplementary Lemma 1 supplies geometric justification for the mean-point construction, while the noise experiments expose its approximation error. The network architecture and training settings are also described.
weaknesses: The claimed advantage under limited computation is only partially established. Figure 3 and the supplementary outlier plots compare RANSAC iterations, although hypothesis costs differ substantially: Table 1 reports 218.71 microseconds for the mean-plus-shift solver versus 77.90 for 5pt+P3P, with learned variants costing more. Equal-iteration improvements therefore do not directly establish the claimed advantage under equal time budgets. The standard five-point baseline also achieves higher AUC on both real calibrated scenes.

The evaluation does not measure all quantities required for the claimed three-camera reconstruction. Its angular metric checks rotations and translation directions for pairs 1–2 and 1–3, but omits their relative translation scale. No focal-length error is reported for 4p3vf. Consequently, the KITTI pose results do not establish accurate recovery of the complete partially calibrated solution, particularly given the restricted stereo-plus-adjacent-frame configuration.

The approximation's operating limits remain insufficiently characterized. Lemma 1 bounds virtual-point distance by a quantity proportional to triangle size; it does not guarantee small pose error. Figure 6 shows appreciable errors even with noiseless inputs. Results stratified by viewpoint change, depth variation, or triangle geometry are absent, leaving uncertainty about when the approximation supplies a reliable initialization.

The learned method contains a concrete mathematical ambiguity: Eq. (2) has a signed numerator without an absolute value or square. Minimizing that expression does not generally minimize epipolar error. Whether this is a transcription error or the implemented objective is unresolved. Moreover, the learned variants provide only small, inconsistent improvements over the much cheaper mean-based alternatives.

Reproduction of the reported results is hindered by missing RANSAC thresholds, stopping settings, and local-refinement details, as well as an unspecified KITTI subset size and sequence selection. Code availability is promised rather than supplied in the manuscript. These are reporting limitations distinct from the empirical contribution of the simple mean-based solver.
